work.author: Alcuin of York
work.description: Two hundred and eighty short questions on Genesis with their answers, gathered for Sigewulf out of Augustine, Jerome, Isidore and Bede. Alcuin's preface says what it is not: the hardest questions in the book are left alone, and what is here is mostly historical and answerable in a sentence, because a traveller cannot carry the weight of books. Many questions name the verse they are about and many do not.
work.title: Interrogationes et responsiones in Genesim
